question: ChatGPT’s designation as a very large online search engine subjects its provider to systemic risk obligations under Articles 34 and 35 of the Digital Services Act (DSA). The AI Act separately establishes obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models, including models classified as presenting systemic risks under Articles 51 and 55 thereof.
Where the same model is used by a designated online search service and other AI functionalities, these frameworks may apply to different aspects of the same technical system. 1.
How does the Commission distinguish service-specific systemic risks under the DSA from model-level systemic risks under the AI Act when both concern the same underlying general-purpose AI model?
What procedures ensure coordination between the Commission’s DSA enforcement services and the AI Office, including where their assessments or proposed mitigation measures differ?

Can compliance with one framework require changes to an AI model that are not required under the other, and how does the Commission prevent conflicting or disproportionate obligations affecting non-designated functionalities?
